entry: Full-contact hybrid martial art and combat sport based on punching and kicking. Bouts take place in a [[Boxing|boxing]] ring, usually with gloves, mouth guards and bare feet to favor kicks. The term kickboxing was introduced in the 1960s by Japanese promoter Osamu Noguchi for a hybrid of [[Muay Thai]] and [[Karate|karate]]. American kickboxing was brought to prominence in September 1974, when the Professional Karate Association (PKA) held the first World Championships. From the 1990s it contributed to [[Mixed martial arts|mixed martial arts]] through hybridization with [[Brazilian jiu-jitsu]] and folk [[Wrestling|wrestling]]. The World Association of Kickboxing Organizations (WAKO) is recognized by the International Olympic Committee as the official world governing body. Professional champion titles are issued by promotions such as Glory and K-1, and rules vary, with some allowing knees or clinching.

Illegal relocation and confinement of a person against their will. A [[Crime|crime]] in many jurisdictions, it may be accomplished by force or fear, or by enticing a victim through [[Fraud|fraud]] or deception, and is distinguished from false imprisonment by the intentional movement of the victim. Kidnapping for ransom is primarily used by larger organizations, such as criminal gangs, terrorist organizations and insurgent groups. It can be accompanied by bodily injury, which in some jurisdictions makes it aggravated kidnapping. Express kidnapping, used mainly in [[Latin America]], demands a small ransom that a family or company can easily pay. Virtual kidnapping is a scam in which callers falsely claim to hold a victim's loved one; around 80 victims were identified, with losses close to $100,000. In the past, and in parts of the world such as southern [[Sudan|Sudan]], kidnapping has been a common means of obtaining slaves and money.

Paired, bean-shaped, blood-filtering organ of the [[Urinary system|urinary system]]. Adult kidneys lie on either side of the spine and are about 12 cm (4½ inches) long. Each receives blood from the renal arteries and is attached to a ureter that carries urine to the [[Bladder|bladder]]. Filtration in the glomerulus removes one-fifth of the blood volume entering the kidney, regulating fluid volume, electrolytes, acid–base balance and toxins. The nephron is the structural and functional unit, and each adult kidney contains around 1 million nephrons. The kidneys also convert a precursor of [[Vitamin D|vitamin D]] to its active form and synthesize the [[Hormone|hormones]] erythropoietin and renin. Kidney failure is treated by dialysis or [[Transplantation (medicine)|transplantation]], almost always once renal function drops below 15%.

British and Canadian actor. He is best known for playing Jack Bauer in the Fox drama series *24*, for which he won a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award. He played President Tom Kirkman in the ABC political drama *Designated Survivor*. His first leading film role was in the Canadian drama *The Bay Boy* (1984). Later films include *Stand by Me* (1986), *The Lost Boys* (1987) and *Flatliners* (1990). He also provided the voice of Venom Snake in *Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain* (2015). He has been inducted into the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].

Canal in northern Germany linking the [[North Sea|North Sea]] and the [[Baltic Sea|Baltic Sea]]. The 98 km (61 mi) freshwater canal runs through [[Schleswig-Holstein]], from Brunsbüttel at the mouth of the [[Elbe]] to Holtenau on the Kiel Fjord. Built between 1887 and 1895 and widened between 1907 and 1914 to admit [[Dreadnought|dreadnought]] battleships, it shortens the sea journey by 460 km (290 mi), bypassing the Jutland peninsula and the Danish Straits. It carries an annual average of 32,000 ships (90 daily), transporting approximately 100 million tonnes of goods. The [[Treaty of Versailles]] required it to be open to vessels of any nation at peace with Germany, but the government under [[Adolf Hitler]] repudiated this status in 1936. The canal was reopened to all traffic after [[World War II]] and took its current name in 1948.

[[Slavs|East Slavic]] state in [[Eastern Europe]], from the late 9th to the mid-13th century. Ruled by the Rurik dynasty, founded by the Varangian prince Rurik, it was an amalgam of principalities that at its greatest extent, in the mid-11th century, stretched from the White Sea to the [[Black Sea|Black Sea]]. [[Vladimir the Great]] spread Christianity, and under [[Yaroslav the Wise]] the state reached its height; his sons issued its first written legal code, *Russkaya Pravda*. The state declined in the late 11th century, splintering into rival principalities, and fell to the Mongol invasion in the mid-13th century. The modern nations of [[Belarus]], [[Russia]] and [[Ukraine]] all claim it as their cultural ancestor.

Capital and largest city of [[Rwanda]] (pop., 2022: 1,745,555), near the country's geographic center. Founded in 1907 as a German administrative outpost, it served as a minor administrative center until it became the national capital at independence in 1962, shifting administrative focus from Huye. The [[Rwandan genocide]] of 1994 killed over 500,000 Tutsi, and the Rwandan Patriotic Front seized Kigali on July 4, 1994. Post-genocide Kigali has experienced rapid population growth, and much of the city has been rebuilt. It is one of the five provinces of Rwanda, divided into three districts, and hosts the president's residence and most government ministries. Its largest contributor to [[Gross domestic product|gross domestic product]] is the service sector.

2011 U.S. military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan. On May 2, 2011, SEAL Team Six shot dead [[Osama bin Laden]], leader of [[Al-Qaeda|al-Qaeda]], in a raid approved by President [[Barack Obama]]. Codenamed Operation Neptune Spear, it was launched from near Jalalabad, Afghanistan. It was supported by over 90% of the American public and welcomed by the [[United Nations]] and [[NATO]]. Al-Qaeda confirmed his death and vowed revenge. It was condemned by two-thirds of the Pakistani public, and Amnesty International questioned why he was not captured alive.

Base unit of mass in the [[International System of Units]] (SI), equal to 1,000 grams. It was defined in 1795, during the [[French Revolution]], as the mass of one [[Litre|liter]] of [[Water|water]] at 0 °C, later adjusted to the temperature of water's maximum density, about 4 °C. From 1889 until 2019 the standard was the International Prototype of the Kilogram, a cylinder of [[Platinum|platinum]]–iridium alloy. The current definition fixes the numerical value of the Planck constant at 6.62607015×10⁻³⁴ J·s, which, with the [[Speed of light|speed of light]] and the cesium-133 transition frequency, defines the mass. The current definition agrees with the original within 30 parts per million. The kilogram is the only SI base unit with an SI prefix in its name.

Unit of length equal to 1,000 meters, from the [[International System of Units|SI]] prefix *kilo-*, meaning one thousand. It is the preferred unit for distances between places on land in most of the world. The notable exceptions are the United States, the United Kingdom and Liberia, where the statute [[Mile|mile]] is used. Although the [[Metre|meter]] was defined in 1799, the myriameter (10,000 meters) was preferred for everyday use. The Dutch adopted the kilometer in 1817 under the local name *mijl*.

American actress. After working as a model, she switched to acting in 1976 and first gained widespread attention as Domino Petachi in the [[James Bond|James Bond]] film *Never Say Never Again* (1983). Her highest-grossing film was *Batman* (1989), in which she played Vicki Vale. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her femme fatale role in *L.A. Confidential* (1997). Her other films include *The Natural* (1984), for which she received a Golden Globe nomination, and *9½ Weeks* (1986). She has a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].

North Korean communist leader (1948–94). He reportedly joined anti-Japanese guerrilla groups and the [[Chinese Communist Party|Chinese Communist Party]] in 1931, and later served in the Soviet [[Red Army|Red Army]]. The [[Soviet Union|Soviet Union]] installed him in power over [[North Korea|North Korea]] after World War II, and in 1948 he founded the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, which he led as a personalist dictatorship with a centrally planned economy. In 1950 he authorized the invasion of South Korea, starting the [[Korean War|Korean War]], which ended in a ceasefire in 1953. He developed the ideology of [[Juche|Juche]], which stressed self-reliance and Korean nationalism. After Soviet aid ended with the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, North Korea suffered famine in 1994. Kim was succeeded by his son [[Kim Jong Il|Kim Jong Il]], establishing the Kim dynasty.

North Korean politician and second supreme leader (1994–2011). He succeeded his father, [[Kim Il Sung|Kim Il Sung]], and ruled as a repressive, totalitarian dictatorship. His Songun, or "military-first," policy made the army the central organizer of civil society. Estimates of deaths in the famine of the 1990s range from 240,000 to over 3 million. He opened the Kaesong Industrial Region in 2003. Under his leadership, North Korea conducted its first nuclear test in 2006. His son, [[Kim Jong Un|Kim Jong Un]], succeeded him.

North Korean politician and supreme leader (since 2011). He is the third ruler of the Kim family to lead North Korea, succeeding his father, [[Kim Jong Il|Kim Jong Il]], in 2011. He is general secretary of the [[Workers' Party of Korea|Workers' Party of Korea]]. His byungjin policy pursues nuclear weapons development alongside economic growth. Kim oversaw the world's four most recent nuclear weapons tests and North Korea's first [[Intercontinental ballistic missile|intercontinental ballistic missile]]. In 2018 and 2019 he met [[Xi Jinping|Xi Jinping]], South Korean president Moon Jae-in and [[Donald Trump|Donald Trump]], but talks broke down without progress on denuclearization.

American media personality and businesswoman. She first gained attention after the 2007 release of a sex tape with singer Ray J, and became known through the [[Reality television|reality]] series *Keeping Up with the Kardashians*, which aired until 2021. She founded the cosmetics line KKW Beauty in 2017 and the shapewear company Skims in 2019, which was valued at over US$4 billion as of 2023. She is the eighth-most-followed individual on [[Instagram|Instagram]]. In 2025 she completed a four-year law apprenticeship but did not pass the California Bar Exam.

British intelligence officer and Soviet double agent. Recruited by Soviet intelligence in 1934 while at Cambridge, he joined the British Secret Intelligence Service ([[MI6|MI6]]) in 1940 and passed large amounts of intelligence to the [[Soviet Union|Soviet Union]]. Suspected of tipping off Guy Burgess and Donald Maclean, who fled to [[Moscow|Moscow]] in 1951, he resigned that year. Publicly cleared in 1955, he resumed work as a journalist and spy in [[Beirut|Beirut]] before being unmasked in 1963 as a member of the Cambridge Five spy ring and defecting to Moscow.

North Korean politician and diplomat. The younger sister of [[Kim Jong Un|Kim Jong Un]] and youngest child of [[Kim Jong Il|Kim Jong Il]], she is believed to be among the most powerful figures in North Korea's political apparatus. As of February 2026, she is director of the General Affairs Department of the [[Workers' Party of Korea|Workers' Party of Korea]], and since March 2026 she has been an alternate member of the Politburo. She has represented North Korea in diplomacy, including at the 2018 Winter Olympics in South Korea.

Traditional Korean side dish (*banchan*) of salted and fermented vegetables, most often [[Cabbage|Chinese cabbage]] or Korean radish. It is seasoned with *gochugaru* (Korean chili powder), spring onions, [[Garlic|garlic]], [[Ginger|ginger]] and salted seafood. Kimchi is a staple eaten with almost every Korean meal, and hundreds of varieties exist, including *baechu-kimchi* and *kkakdugi*. Traditionally, winter kimchi was stored in earthenware fermentation vessels called *onggi*, buried in the ground. The communal making of kimchi, called *gimjang*, is recognized by [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Studio album by American jazz trumpeter [[Miles Davis|Miles Davis]], released on August 17, 1959. Recorded in two sessions in March and April 1959 for [[Columbia Records|Columbia Records]], it features a sextet with [[John Coltrane|John Coltrane]], Julian "Cannonball" Adderley, Bill Evans, Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb. Davis based *Kind of Blue* entirely on modality, giving each musician a set of scales to shape improvisation rather than chord changes, a departure from his earlier hard bop style. Critics regard it as Davis's masterpiece and one of the greatest albums of all time. In 2002 the [[Library of Congress|Library of Congress]] added it to the National Recording Registry, and [[Rolling Stone|Rolling Stone]] ranked it number 12 in 2003 and number 31 in 2020. The Recording Industry Association of America certified it quintuple platinum in 2019, for five million units in the United States.

Branch of physics and geometry describing motion without regard to the [[Force|forces]] that cause it. It specifies the positions and [[Velocity|velocities]] of points and bodies, along with the mathematical transformations between coordinate systems. A problem begins with the geometry of a system and known initial conditions, from which unknown positions, velocities and accelerations are determined. The scholar Ibn al-Haytham is credited with first treating geometry and kinematics as a unified concept. The field is distinguished from dynamics, which studies the effect of forces on bodies. It describes celestial motion in [[Astrophysics|astrophysics]] and multi-link systems in [[Mechanical engineering|mechanical engineering]], [[Robotics|robotics]] and biomechanics, such as engines, robotic arms and the [[Human skeleton|human skeleton]]. Relativistic kinematics, applying special relativity, encompasses [[Time dilation|time dilation]] and the [[Lorentz transformation|Lorentz transformation]].

Energy of a moving physical body, equal to one-half its [[Mass|mass]] times the square of its speed. In classical mechanics, a non-rotating object of mass *m* moving at speed *v* has kinetic energy ½*mv*². This equals the [[Work (physics)|work]] needed to accelerate the object from rest to that speed, and the object does the same amount of work when it decelerates to rest. The SI unit is the [[Joule|joule]]. The formula is a good approximation only when speed is much less than the [[Speed of light|speed of light]]. The term was coined in the mid-19th century by [[Lord Kelvin|William Thomson, later Lord Kelvin]], and the word derives from the Greek *kinesis*, meaning motion.

Legendary king of Britain and central figure in the medieval literary tradition known as the Matter of Britain. Early Welsh sources portray him as a leader of the post-Roman Britons against the [[Anglo-Saxons|Anglo-Saxons]] in the late 5th and early 6th centuries, but his earliest mentions appear about 300 years after he is supposed to have lived. Most historians do not regard him as a historical figure. The 9th-century *Historia Brittonum* lists twelve battles that he fought. Geoffrey of Monmouth's 12th-century *Historia Regum Britanniae* made Arthur internationally known, adding [[Merlin|Merlin]], Guinevere, the sword [[Excalibur|Excalibur]] and Arthur's final battle against Mordred. [[Chrétien de Troyes|Chrétien de Troyes]] added Lancelot and the [[Holy Grail|Holy Grail]], beginning the genre of Arthurian romance. The legend varies widely between texts, revived in the 19th century, and remains prominent in film, television and [[Comics|comics]].

English progressive rock band formed in London in 1968. Guitarist Robert Fripp was its primary composer and sole constant member. The band helped shape the progressive rock movement, influencing [[Yes (band)|Yes]] and [[Genesis (band)|Genesis]]. Its debut album, *In the Court of the Crimson King* (1969), is widely cited as a cornerstone of the genre. After Fripp disbanded the group in 1974, it returned in 1981 and recorded *Discipline* (1981), *Beat* (1982) and *Three of a Perfect Pair* (1984). The band permanently ceased activity after a December 2021 tour, when Fripp said it had moved from sound to silence.

English translation of the [[Bible|Bible]], published in 1611. Commissioned by King James VI and I after the Hampton Court Conference of 1604, it was the third English translation approved by the [[Church of England|Church of England]]. Noted for its "majesty of style," it has remained in continuous use for over four centuries and shaped [[Hymn|hymnody]], [[Liturgy|liturgy]] and everyday English idioms. The 1769 Oxford edition is the standard text that the unqualified title usually denotes. With stereotype printing in the early 19th century, it became the most widely printed book in history.

Tragedy by [[William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare]], written in late 1605 or early 1606. Set in pre-Roman Britain, the play depicts an aging king who divides his kingdom according to his daughters' professions of love. When his youngest daughter, Cordelia, refuses to flatter him, he disinherits her, and his descent into madness unleashes betrayal and civil strife. The earliest known performance was on St. Stephen's Day in 1606. The play survives in the 1608 quarto, the 1619 quarto and the 1623 First Folio, which differ significantly. Nahum Tate's 1681 revision, with a romantic subplot and a less bleak ending, displaced Shakespeare's version from the stage until 1838. In *A Defence of Poetry* (1821), [[Percy Bysshe Shelley|Percy Bysshe Shelley]] called it "the most perfect specimen of the dramatic art existing in the world."
